name: Pallas
tagline: The belt's tilted giant — a basaltic protoplanet diving through the planetary plane.

facts.label: Inclination
facts.value: 34.8° — the belt's most tilted major orbit

history: Pallas was the second asteroid ever found, discovered just a year after Ceres. Its orbit is tipped a dramatic 34.8 degrees off the ecliptic — so steep that no spacecraft has ever visited it. VLT imagery revealed a heavily cratered basaltic surface, suggesting Pallas survived one of the most violent bombardment histories in the belt. Like Vesta it is a leftover protoplanet, too small to finish differentiating before the Solar System's formation window closed.
